validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + SPEC confirmed by two independent sources -- this is NOT a GEM-only entity. (1) OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012, Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', Libya section, p.75 (matches the wiki page's own citation, cite_note-1): row 'Tripoli/Mellitah | Sirte Oil | 98 [miles] | 34 [in] | 16,992,353 [1,000 scm/yr] | na'. 98 mi = 157.7 km, matching GEM's LengthKnown=158.00 km almost exactly; diameter 34 in matches GEM's Diameter=34.00 in exactly; capacity 16,992,353 thousand scm/yr = 16.992 bcm/yr, matching GEM's Capacity=16.99 bcm/y essentially exactly. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THIS LINK: the currently-cited live URL (https://www.opec.org/opec_web/static_files_project/media/downloads/publications/ASB2012.pdf) is DEAD -- it now 200s to the OPEC homepage HTML, not the PDF (confirmed via curl: file type is HTML, not PDF). I substituted the Wayback Machine snapshot (2025-01-10), confirmed via `file` to be a genuine PDF (v1.6) and via `pdftotext` to contain 'Tripoli/Mellitah ... 98 ... 34 ... 16,992,353' verbatim in Table 4.10. url_verifier's automated substring check FALSE-NEGATIVES on this Wayback PDF URL ('FAIL 200 but missing expected') because it can't extract text from this PDF's encoding via a naive byte scan -- this is the documented PDF false-negative pattern in the tool's own docstring; I verified manually with pdftotext (confirmed content) and curl (confirmed live 200) before citing. (2) alwasatnews.com (Bahraini newspaper), 2006-08-23, 'Bong Lloyd wins contract to implement Tripoli gas line project in Libya': the contract (Sirte Oil and Gas Production Co., chairman Ahmed Aoun, vs Bong Lloyd/Atul Bung) covered two projects -- an Al-Khums-Tripoli line (126 km + 32 km branches, 106 mmcf/d, feeds Tripoli's south power station) AND, separately and explicitly, a 'Tripoli to Mellitah Pipeline' (200 mmcf/d incremental capacity for this construction phase) feeding the Zawiya power station west of Tripoli, with pressure-reduction/gas-measurement/compression infrastructure at Mellitah. This independently corroborates the pipeline's existence, route (Tripoli->Mellitah), operator (Sirte Oil, matching OPEC), and rough construction vintage (mid-2000s buildout/expansion). The 200 mmcf/d figure is NOT a spec conflict with GEM's 16.99 bcm/y (~1,643 mmcf/d): the article describes only the incremental capacity added by the 2006 construction contract, not the trunk's cumulative/full design capacity as later reported by OPEC for 2011. CLASSIFICATION: correct -- a gas transmission trunk line supplying a power station, not a gathering/process line, consistent with both sources. DUPLICATE check against the full 30-pipeline roster: no other entry matches P1865's length/diameter/capacity combination (158 km / 34 in / 16.99 bcm/y is unique); this segment sits within the broader corridor also tracked in aggregate as P0483 'Libya Coastal Gas Pipeline' (Mellitah->Benghazi, 1164 km), but OPEC's own table treats Tripoli/Mellitah as its own distinct row alongside Khoms/Tripoli (P1864), Brega/Khoms (P1863) and Brega/Benghazi (P1862) -- so GEM's segment-level tracking mirrors the primary source's own segmentation, not a double-count/relabel of P0483 or any other roster pipeline. ATTRIBUTION nuance (not an error): GEM's Owner1 is 'Libyan National Oil Corp' (100%); both independent sources name the direct operator as 'Sirte Oil' / Sirte Oil and Gas Production Co., a wholly NOC-owned subsidiary confirmed still active in gas transport as of recent (2024) reporting -- recording the parent (NOC) as owner is defensible, but the sheet could add Sirte Oil Company as operator if a separate field exists. STATUS: 'operating' is corroborated beyond the 2011 OPEC snapshot -- independent 2024-2025 reporting (Libya Observer, MEES) confirms the Mellitah-Zawiya-Tripoli gas corridor remains a live, physically real piece of infrastructure (armed-group pipeline closures/restorations at the Zawiya power station in 2025; NOC restoring coastal gas-line flows to Tripoli-area power stations in 2024), so the segment has not gone derelict since the 2011/2006 sourcing. Side note (out of scope for this row, flagged only for awareness): cross-checking the same OPEC table surfaced an apparent unit-conversion bug in a DIFFERENT roster row -- P1863 'Brega-Khoms' is listed by OPEC as 645 MILES (=1,038 km) but GEM records LengthKnown=645.00 km, i.e. the raw mileage figure appears to have been entered as km without conversion. Not corrected here since it's outside P1865's row.

summary: P1865 Tripoli-Mellitah Gas Pipeline: confirmed (caveat) -- existence, spec (158km/34in/16.99bcm/y), and classification all corroborated near-exactly by OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (via Wayback, live opec.org URL is dead) plus a 2006 alwasatnews.com construction-contract article that explicitly names the 'Tripoli to Mellitah Pipeline' feeding the Zawiya power station; no duplicate/existence/classification problem. Minor attribution nuance: sources name operator 'Sirte Oil' (NOC subsidiary) vs sheet's Owner1='Libyan National Oil Corp' -- not a conflict, just imprecise.
